speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific movements you are experiencing and when you first noticed them?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are you experiencing any involuntary muscle stiffness, tremors, or a feeling of restlessness that makes it difficult to sit still? Has this started gradually or did it appear suddenly after starting the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: This presentation is classic for akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes, do you feel an inner sense of anxiety or discomfort that drives this restlessness, and does the urge to move temporarily relieve that feeling?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the inner sense of restlessness that is temporarily relieved by movement; this subjective experience is the hallmark of akathisia. Given the clear temporal relationship with starting risperidone two months ago and the absence of other medical or substance-related causes, no further tests are needed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia secondary to risperidone
